place: Sant'Alfio and Mascali, eastern slope of Mount Etna, Sicily
note: THREE FULLY VERIFIED TREES WITH NO HOME YET, and that is the only thing wrong with them. They came out of a Taormina verify pass on 2026-08-30 and they are not in Taormina: all three stand 18 to 19 km away on Etna's eastern slope, in Sant'Alfio and Mascali, which is well beyond the day-trip boundary of roughly 30 minutes by public transport. Publishing them under Taormina would have been exactly what that rule forbids, presenting an out-of-town tree as standing in the city, and it would have been the whole page, because every one of Taormina's own five register trees is blocked on private hotel grounds (see data/leads/taormina.json). Catania, the nearest published city, is 28 km away, which is no better. WHAT TO DO WITH THEM, and one route is closed. A COLLECTION ENTRY DOES NOT WORK: collection entries are {city_slug, tree_id} pairs pointing at a tree that is already published, so a collection cannot give a tree its first home. Checked 2026-08-30 rather than assumed, because the first version of this note recommended exactly that and would have sent the next run down a dead end. What is left is two routes, both real. (1) A Sant'Alfio page of its own once four trees clear the bar on that slope; these three are already three of them, and Etna's eastern slope is dense with chestnuts, so a fourth is likely cheap. (2) Hidde rules that the day-trip boundary stretches for Catania, which is his call and not a run's. The Hundred-Horse Chestnut is worth the trouble either way: roughly 2,200 years on a 2022 CREA study, one of the most famous trees in the world, free to visit, and confirmed alive by the comune's own page in March 2026. Do not re-verify any of this, it is done and sourced.
verified: 2026-08-30, session pass, sources and pins intact below

trees.name: The Hundred-Horse Chestnut

location.neighbourhood: Sant'Alfio, eastern slope of Mount Etna (day-trip from Taormina, not in-town)

trees.access: Free, no entry cost, open all year (comune.santalfio.ct.it, last updated 2026-03-26). Some steps at the entrance may not suit wheelchair users. This is a day trip from Taormina, not a walk from town.
trees.transport: About 19km straight-line from Taormina centre, on Etna's eastern slope above Sant'Alfio. Roughly 45 minutes to an hour by car via the SP59/mountain roads; no practical public transport connection, so a car or taxi is the realistic way to reach it.
trees.verify_notes: Known as the Castagno dei Cento Cavalli. This candidate is NOT the same as the staged register row of the same distance band; its coordinates (37.750183, 15.130367) match the tree-level Wikipedia coordinate (37deg45'00.6"N 15deg07'49.28"E) almost exactly, and the register's own address (Via Castagno 100 Cavalli) confirms identity. Legend: a queen and her hundred mounted knights sheltered from a storm under it. Physically three huge fused stems (10.5m, 23m, 23.6m) from one root system rather than three separate trees, which the story should make clear so a visitor is not confused. Girth: register gives 2200cm/22m, Wikipedia gives approx 23m circumference (1780 survey with branches included gave 57.9m) -- consistent, minor rounding difference, not a conflict worth flagging. Age: a 2022 C.R.E.A. dendrological study put it at 2,200 years (cited identically by Wikipedia and the comune's own page, both updated within the last year, so treated as two corroborating citations of one study rather than two independent measurements); older folklore/botanical estimates ranged 2,000-4,000 years, kept as the outer band. Damaged by fire in 1923 (recorded on Wikipedia); treated for bark canker (Fusarium) by volunteer arborists per a widely reported 2023 restoration, per a WebSearch summary of an ANSA article that itself sits behind ANSA's cookie/subscription wall and could not be fetched directly -- flagging this specific claim as a lead rather than a verified fact, though the tree's current alive status is independently confirmed by the comune's own page, last updated 2026-03-26. Designated a National Monument in 1965, UNESCO 'Monument Messenger of Peace' 2006, Italian Tree of the Year 2021, one of only 150 trees of exceptional value the State Forestry Corps singled out from 22,000 in 1982. No other MASAF/Sicilian-register candidate stands within a kilometre of it; it is a lone destination rather than part of a walkable cluster.
trees.resolved: PUBLISHED 2026-08-31 as sal_001 on the Sant'Alfio page, under Hidde's same-day ruling that a place may publish below four trees when one tree is itself the destination. Do not re-verify. The other two entries here are still leads.

trees.name: The Ship's Chestnut

location.address: Beside the path/road from the Castagno dei Cento Cavalli, about 500m further uphill, on the Sant'Alfio/Mascali boundary
location.neighbourhood: Carpineto, Mascali, eastern slope of Mount Etna (same day-trip as the Hundred-Horse Chestnut)

trees.access: Stands on private land, but directly at the edge of the road/path, described by the source as 'ben visibile' (clearly visible) without entering the property. Free, no ticket, reached on foot from the Cento Cavalli in about 500m.
trees.transport: Same trip as the Hundred-Horse Chestnut, about 500m further along the same path. Roughly 45 minutes to an hour by car from Taormina; no practical public transport.
trees.verify_notes: Called the Castagno della Nave (nicknamed 'arusbigghiasonnu', roughly 'wakes-you-from-sleep', for the racket of the hundreds of birds it hosts); its trunk base is said to resemble a ship's hull, hence the name. NOT the same register row as the staged 'Tramazzi' candidate (04/I216/CT/19, girth 860cm) -- coordinates are about 2.5km apart, so these are two different trees; this one is listed under a separate, newer Sicilian regional-register sheet, 01/F004/CT/19 (decree D.D.G. n. 2856 of 2025-10-13, per etnanatura.it, comune given as Mascali not Sant'Alfio), which I could not fetch directly to confirm the decree text itself. Coordinates are DMS-to-decimal converted from etnanatura.it's own trail data (37deg45'15"N 15deg07'52"E, rounded to the nearest arc-second, roughly 20-30m of slack) rather than a register-precise pin, hence 'approximate' rather than 'confirmed'. Height ~20m stated directly on the source page ('alto quasi venti metri'); no girth figure appears on the page I fetched, so girth_cm is left empty rather than repeating an unverified 'circumference of 20 metres' figure that only appeared in a search-engine AI summary and could not be confirmed on the page itself (the search-summary-is-a-lead-not-a-source rule). Age: page states 'vecchio di 1.800 anni' (1,800 years old) as a specific figure from one source; a second source (go-etna.it) only corroborates 'millenary'/over a thousand years without a precise figure, hence flagged as thin on the exact number rather than in conflict. An unconfirmed claim (via search summary) says both this tree and the Cento Cavalli were jointly protected by a 1745 Sicilian royal heritage-tribunal act; not independently verified, included here only as a lead for the writer.

trees.name: The Etna Birch of Magazzeni

location.address: Magazzeni, Sant'Alfio, eastern slope of Mount Etna, approx. 1010m altitude
location.neighbourhood: Sant'Alfio, near Monti Sartorius, in the same day-trip zone as the two chestnuts

verified_sources: Regione Siciliana, 'Elenco degli alberi monumentali di Sicilia', updated 2024-11-07 (same sheet code and near-identical coordinates; PDF at regione.sicilia.it 404'd on direct fetch, cited via a search-engine snippet quoting the document's own table -- see verify_notes)
trees.access: Free, on the wooded upper slopes of Etna within Sant'Alfio's territory. I found no explicit statement of a marked public path to this specific tree (unlike the two chestnuts, which have named trails); it sits in open forest at 1010m rather than behind any gate or private boundary, but this pass could not independently confirm a walking route. Flagged rather than stated as certain.
trees.transport: About 19.4km straight-line from Taormina, in the same Etna day-trip area as the two Sant'Alfio chestnuts (a few km apart, drivable together). No practical public transport; a car is needed.
trees.verify_notes: Betula aetnensis is a glacial-relict endemic found only on Etna's north/northeast/northwest slopes (1450-2000m is the typical birch-forest band; this individually-registered specimen sits lower, at 1010m, per both registers). Its bark is unusually pale because the arid, lava-ash environment carries too little lichen to darken the trunk (a detail repeated across sources, worth the story). Monumentality here rests on rarity/endemism and landscape value rather than great age -- no age source was found for this individual and none should be invented; leave age fields empty and let the page ask the reader if anyone has more on this specimen. Girth (205cm) and height (12m) are corroborated by an exact coordinate match between the MASAF national register (already in the staged supply file) and a second, separately published Sicilian regional catalogue -- I could not open the regional PDF directly (404 on the published URL) so this second citation rests on a search-engine snippet quoting that document's table rather than my own view of the page; the fact that the quoted coordinates match our own staged data to six decimal places is strong circumstantial evidence the snippet is reproducing the real table rather than inventing figures, but it falls short of a directly-fetched second source, hence flagged. Treat as needing one more independent source (a news piece, a hiking blog with photos of this specific tree) before this leaves 'flagged'.
